latin_text: In the first world, God, the primal unity, presides over nine orders of angels as if over as many spheres and, without moving, moves all toward himself.
english_translation: In the first world, God, the primal unity, presides over nine orders of angels as if over as many spheres and, without moving, moves all toward himself.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico establishes the fundamental correspondence: God as primal unity presides over nine angelic orders in the intelligible realm, *without moving*, yet moving all toward himself through love and intellection. This parallels the empyrean presiding over nine celestial spheres and matter informing nine spheres of sublunary being. [INFERRED] The phrase "without moving, moves all" captures the paradox of divine causality—God is absolutely transcendent yet absolutely active. Angels, as the first-emanated, immediately experience this movement toward divine unity as their eternal return.

The philosophical function is structural: the ninefold correspondence (9 orders = 9 spheres = 9 sublunary realms) establishes that identical principles govern all levels of reality. This justifies both mysticism (ascending through the nine orders means ascending toward God) and natural magic (understanding the nine celestial spheres means understanding angelic governance). [INFERRED] The correspondence is not merely symbolic but ontological—the nine orders structurally shape the cosmos itself.

[INFERRED] Commento Book III (C.3.2) develops this ninefold structure explicitly. The Oration (O.1.11) invokes Jacob's Ladder as the same structure. Being & Unity grounds it: each degree of participated being corresponds to an angelic order.
notes: HARVESTER passage: H.SP.3 | Nine orders of angels; angelic spheres as mirrors of celestial and elemental orders
